description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Anna Canale. In the paper we state conditions on potentials V V to get the improved Hardy inequality with weight c N , μ ​ ∫ ℝ N φ 2 | x | 2 ​ μ ​ ( x ) ​ 𝑑 x + ∫ ℝ N V φ 2 μ ( x ) d x ≤ ∫ ℝ N | ∇ φ | 2 ​ μ ​ ( x ) ​ d x + C μ ​ ∫ ℝ N φ 2 ​

title: The Curse of Unrolling: Rate of Differentiating Through Optimization
creator: Damien Scieur, Quentin Bertrand, Gauthier Gidel, Fabian Pedregosa
description: Abstract Computing the Jacobian of the solution of an optimization problem is a central problem in machine learning, with applications in hyperparameter optimization, meta-learning, optimization as a layer, and dataset distillation, to name a few. Unrolled differentiation is a popular heuristic that approximates the solution using an iterative solver and differentiates it through the computational path.

title: A panchromatic view of infrared quasars: excess star formation and radio emission in the most heavily obscured systems 2015 A panchromatic view of infrared quasars: excess star formation and radio emission in the most heavily obscured systems –
creator: Carolina Andonie, David M. Alexander, David Rosario, Brivael Laloux, Antonis Georgakakis, Leah K. Morabito, Carolin Villforth, Mathilda Avirett-Mackenzie, Gabriela Calistro Rivera, Agnese Del Moro, Sotiria Fotopoulou, Chris Harrison, Andrea Lapi, James Petley, Grayson Petter, and Francesco Shankar
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Carolina Andonie, David M. Alexander, David Rosario, Brivael Laloux, Antonis Georgakakis, Leah K. Morabito, Carolin Villforth, Mathilda Avirett-Mackenzie, Gabriela Calistro Rivera, Agnese Del Moro, Sotiria Fotopoulou, Chris Harrison, Andrea Lapi, James Petley, Grayson Petter, and Francesco Shankar. To understand the Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) phenomenon and their impact on the evolution of galaxies, a complete AGN census is required; however, finding heavily obscured AGNs is observationally challenging.

title: DELTAR: Depth Estimation from a Light-weight ToF Sensor and RGB Image
creator: Yijin Li, Xinyang Liu, Wenqi Dong, Han Zhou, Hujun Bao, Guofeng Zhang, Yinda Zhang *, Zhaopeng Cui
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yijin Li, Xinyang Liu, Wenqi Dong, Han Zhou, Hujun Bao, Guofeng Zhang, Yinda Zhang *, Zhaopeng Cui. Light-weight time-of-flight (ToF) depth sensors are small, cheap, low-energy and have been massively deployed on mobile devices for the purposes like autofocus, obstacle detection, etc. However, due to their specific measurements (depth distribution in a region instead of the depth value at a certain pixel) and extremely low resolution, they are insufficient for applications requiring high-fidelity depth such as 3D reconstruction.

title: OBBStacking: An Ensemble Method for Remote Sensing Object Detection PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
creator: Haoning Lin, Changhao Sun, Yunpeng Liu
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Haoning Lin, Changhao Sun, Yunpeng Liu. Ensemble methods are a reliable way to combine several models to achieve superior performance. However, research on the application of ensemble methods in the remote sensing object detection scenario is mostly overlooked. First, one unique characteristic of remote sensing object detection is the Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) of the objects and the fusion of multiple OBBs requires further research attention.

title: Slow and fast particles in shear-driven jamming: critical behavior and finite size scaling
creator: Peter Olsson
description: Abstract We do shear-driven simulations of a simple model of non-Brownian particles in two dimensions. By examining the velocity distribution at different densities and shear rates we find strong evidence for the existence of two different processes, respectively dominated by the slower and the faster particles—the slow process and the fast process.

title: BiFold: A Python code for the calculation of double folded (bifold) potentials with density-in/dependent nucleon-nucleon interactions Journal: Computer Physics Communications
creator: Mesut Karakoç
description: Abstract BiFold calculates the density-dependent (DDM3Y n n , BDM3Y n n , CDM3Y n n ) or independent double folded potentials between two colliding spherical nuclei. It is written in a Python package form to give the ability to use the potentials directly in a nuclear reaction/structure code.

title: Performance of a prototype TORCH time-of-flight detector
creator: S. Bhasin, T. Blake, N. H. Brook, M. F. Cicala, T. Conneely, D. Cussans, M. W. U. van Dijk, R. Forty, C. Frei, E. P. M. Gabriel, R. Gao, T. Gershon, T. Gys, T. Hadavizadeh, T. H. Hancock, N. Harnew, T. Jones, M. Kreps, J. Milnes, D. Piedigrossi, J. Rademacker, J. C. Smallwood
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by S. Bhasin, T. Blake, N. H. Brook, M. F. Cicala, T. Conneely, D. Cussans, M. W. U. van Dijk, R. Forty, C. Frei, E. P. M. Gabriel, R. Gao, T. Gershon, T. Gys, T. Hadavizadeh, T. H. Hancock, N. Harnew, T. Jones, M. Kreps, J. Milnes, D. Piedigrossi, J. Rademacker, J. C. Smallwood.

title: Bounds for the reduction number of primary ideal in dimension three
creator: Mousumi Mandal and Kumari Saloni
description: Abstract . Let ( R , 𝔪 ) (R,\mathfrak{m}) be a Cohen-Macaulay local ring of dimension d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 and I I an 𝔪 \mathfrak{m} -primary ideal of R R . Let r J ​ ( I ) r_{J}(I) be the reduction number of I I with respect to a minimal reduction J J of I I .

title: Regular covariant representations and their Wold-type decomposition Thanks: *corresponding author
creator: Azad Rohilla, Harsh Trivedi, Shankar Veerabathiran *
description: Abstract . Olofsson introduced a growth condition regarding elements of an orbit for an expansive operator and generalized Richter’s wandering subspace theorem. Later on, using the Moore-Penrose inverse, Ezzahraoui, Mbekhta, and Zerouali extended the growth condition and obtained a Shimorin-Wold-type decomposition.

title: Radiation-free and non-Hermitian topology inertial defect states of on-chip magnons
creator: Bowen Zeng, Tao Yu
description: Abstract Radiative damping is a strong dissipation source for the quantum emitters hybridized with propagating photons, electrons, or phonons, which is not easily avoidable for on-chip magnonic emitters as well that can radiate via the surface acoustic waves of the substrate.

title: The quasi bound spectrum of H 2
creator: E. M. Roueff a and H. Abgrall a
description: Abstract We compute the radiative ro-vibrational emission spectrum of H 2 involving quasibound states via a simple numerical method of resolution of the Schrödinger equation by introducing a modified effective molecular potential. The comparison of the eigenvalues obtained with our approximation and other theoretical methods based on scattering resonance properties is excellent.

title: Is your forecaster smarter than an energy engineer: a deep dive into electricity price forecasting
creator: Maria Margarida Mascarenhas, Hussain Kazmi
description: Abstract The field of electricity price forecasting has seen significant advances in the last years, including the development of new, more accurate forecast models. These models leverage statistical relationships in previously observed data to predict the future; however, there is a lack of analysis explaining these models, which limits their real world applicability in critical infrastructure.

title: Strong single-photon to two-photon bundles emission in spin-1 Jaynes-Cummings model
creator: Jing Tang 1 and Yuangang Deng 1,∗
description: Abstract The realization of high-quality special nonclassical states beyond strong single atom-cavity coupling regime is a fundamental element in quantum information science. Here, we study the nonclassical photon emission in a single spin-1 atom coupled to an optical cavity with constructing a spin-1 Jaynes-Cummings model.

title: Semigroup intersection problems in the Heisenberg groups
creator: Ruiwen Dong
description: Abstract We consider two algorithmic problems concerning sub-semigroups of Heisenberg groups and, more generally, two-step nilpotent groups. The first problem is Intersection Emptiness , which asks whether a finite number of given finitely generated semigroups have empty intersection. This problem was first studied by Markov in the 1940s.

title: The gravity of light
creator: Jan W. van Holten
description: Abstract The gravitational field of an idealized plane-wave solution of the Maxwell equations can be described in closed form. After discussing this particular solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations, the motion of neutral test particles, which are sensitive only to the gravitational background field, is analyzed.

title: Discriminating power of milli-lensing observations for dark matter models
creator: Nick Loudas, Vasiliki Pavlidou, Carolina Casadio, Konstantinos Tassis
description: Abstract Context. The nature of dark matter (DM) is still under intense debate. Sub-galactic scales are particularly critical, as different, currently viable DM models make diverse predictions on the expected abundance and density profile of DM haloes on these scales. Aims.

title: Family Non-universal Z ′ Z^{\prime} Effects on B d , s → K ∗ 0 ​ K ¯ ∗ 0 B_{d,s}\to K^{*0}{\overline{K}^{*0}} Decays in Perturbative QCD Approach
creator: Ying Li, Guo-Hua Zhao, Yan-Jun Sun, Zhi-Tian Zou
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ying Li, Guo-Hua Zhao, Yan-Jun Sun, Zhi-Tian Zou. The nonleptonic decays B d , s → K ∗ 0 ​ K ¯ ∗ 0 B_{d,s}\to K^{*0}{\overline{K}^{*0}} are reanalyzed in perturbative QCD approach, which is based on the k T k_{\rm T} factorization.

title: Graph Neural Network Expressivity and Meta-Learning for Molecular Property Regression
creator: Yanqiao Zhu, Yuanqi Du
description: Abstract We demonstrate the applicability of model-agnostic algorithms for meta-learning, specifically Reptile, to GNN models in molecular regression tasks. Using meta-learning we are able to learn new chemical prediction tasks with only a few model updates, as compared to using randomly initialized GNNs which require learning each regression task from scratch.

title: Solving homogeneous linear equations over polynomial semirings
creator: Ruiwen Dong
description: Abstract For a subset B B of ℝ \mathbb{R} , denote by U ⁡ ( B ) \operatorname{U}(B) be the semiring of (univariate) polynomials in ℝ ⁡ [ X ] \mathbb{R}[X] that are strictly positive on B B . Let ℕ ⁡ [ X ] \mathbb{N}[X] be the semiring of (univariate) polynomials with non-negative integer coefficients.

title: InSight Pressure Data Recalibration, and its Application to the Study of Long-Term Pressure Changes on Mars
description: Abstract Observations of the South Polar Residual Cap suggest a possible erosion of the cap, leading to an increase of the global mass of the atmosphere. We test this assumption by making the first comparison between Viking 1 and InSight surface pressure data, which were recorded 40 years apart.

title: Tropical computations for toric intersection theory in Macaulay2
creator: Alessio Borzì
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alessio Borzì. We present the Macaulay2 package TropicalToric.m2 for toric intersection theory computations using tropical geometry. 1 Introduction Toric varieties are ubiquitous in algebraic geometry. Their intersection theory was first studied in Fulton and Sturmfels [ fulton1997toricintersection ] , and it has many applications in different contexts, including: wonderful and tropical compactifications [ tevelev2007compactification , deconcini1995wonderful , feichtner2004chow ] , birational geometry [ gibeny2010equations , gibeny2012bounds , castravet2020blown ] , tropical geometry [ katz2011realization ] , tropical intersection theory [ katz2009toolkit , osserman2013lifting ,

title: Signatures of quantum geometry from exponential corrections to the black hole entropy
creator: 𝐒𝐨𝐡𝐚𝐦 \mathbf{Soham} 𝐒𝐞𝐧 a † \mathbf{Sen}^{a\dagger} , 𝐀𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐬 \mathbf{Ashis} 𝐒𝐚𝐡𝐚 a , b ∗ \mathbf{Saha}^{a,b*} and 𝐒𝐮𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐧 \mathbf{Sunandan} 𝐆𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐨𝐩𝐚𝐝𝐡𝐲𝐚𝐲 a ‡ \mathbf{Gangopadhyay}^{a\ddagger}
description: Abstract It has been recently shown in [ Phys. Rev. Lett. 125 (2020) 041302 ] that microstate counting carried out for quantum states residing on the horizon of a black hole leads to a correction of the form exp ( − A / 4 l p 2 ) \exp(-A/4l_{p}^{2}) in the Bekenstein-Hawking form of the black hole entropy.

title: Exact augmented lagrangian duality for mixed integer convex optimization
creator: Avinash Bhardwaj, Vishnu Narayanan, Abhishek Pathapati
description: Abstract Augmented Lagrangian dual augments the classical Lagrangian dual with a non-negative non-linear penalty function of the violation of the relaxed/dualized constraints in order to reduce the duality gap. We investigate the cases in which mixed integer convex optimization problems have an exact penalty representation using sharp augmenting functions (norms as augmenting penalty functions).

title: Bottom hadro-chemistry in high-energy hadronic collisions
creator: Min He 1 and Ralf Rapp 2
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Min He 1 and Ralf Rapp 2. The hadro-chemistry of bottom quarks ( b b ) produced in hadronic collisions encodes valuable information on the mechanism of color-neutralization in these reactions. Since the b b -quark mass is much larger than the typical hadronic scale of ∼ \sim 1 GeV, b ​ b ¯ b\bar{b} pair production is expected to be well separated from subsequent hadronization processes.

title: UAV-based Visual Remote Sensing for Automated Building Inspection
creator: Kushagra Srivastava, Dhruv Patel ⋆ \star, Aditya Kumar Jha, Mohhit Kumar Jha, Jaskirat Singh, Ravi Kiran Sarvadevabhatla, Pradeep Kumar Ramancharla, Harikumar Kandath, K. Madhava Krishna
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kushagra Srivastava, Dhruv Patel ⋆ \star, Aditya Kumar Jha, Mohhit Kumar Jha, Jaskirat Singh, Ravi Kiran Sarvadevabhatla, Pradeep Kumar Ramancharla, Harikumar Kandath, K. Madhava Krishna. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) based remote sensing system incorporated with computer vision has demonstrated potential for assisting building construction and in disaster management like damage assessment during earthquakes.

title: Resource Allocation for Mobile Metaverse with the Internet of Vehicles over 6G Wireless Communications: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
creator: Terence Jie Chua, Wenhan Yu, Jun Zhao
description: Abstract Improving the interactivity and interconnectivity between people is one of the highlights of the Metaverse. The Metaverse relies on a core approach, digital twinning, which is a means to replicate physical world objects, people, actions and scenes onto the virtual world.

title: On general-relativistic Lagrangian perturbation theory and its non-perturbative generalization
creator: Thomas Buchert *, Ismael Delgado Gaspar, Jan J. Ostrowski
description: Abstract The Newtonian Lagrangian perturbation theory is a widely used framework to study structure formation in cosmology in the nonlinear regime. We review a general-relativistic formulation of such a perturbation approach, emphasizing results on already developed extensive formalism including among other aspects: the non-perturbative modeling of Ricci and Weyl curvatures, gravitational waves and pressure-supported fluids.

title: Iterated Integrals associated with colored rooted trees
creator: Hanamichi Kawamura
description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce iterated integrals associated with colored rooted trees and give proofs for the shuffle relations for 𝒑 \boldsymbol{p} -adic finite and t t -adic symmetric polylogarithms. This method generalizes the theory of the finite multiple zeta values associated with 2 2 -colored rooted trees introduced by Ono. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 11M32, 05C05. 1.

title: Lattice Fluid Dynamics: Thirty-five Years Down the Road
creator: Sauro Succi (1) Center for Life Nano-Neuro Science at La Sapienza,Italian Institute of Technology, Viale Regina Elena 295, 00161, Roma, Italy,(2) Physics Department, Harvard University,Oxford Str 17, 02138, Cambridge, USA,(3) Mechanical Engineering Department,University College London,Gower Street,
description: Abstract We comment on the role and impact of lattice fluid dynamics on the general landscape of computational fluid dynamics. Starting from the historical development of Lattice Gas Cellular Automata, we move on to a cursory appraisal of the main applications of the Lattice Boltzmann method and challenges ahead.

title: Reinforcement Learning with Non-Exponential Discounting
creator: Matthias Schultheis, Constantin A. Rothkopf, Heinz Koeppl
description: Abstract Commonly in reinforcement learning (RL), rewards are discounted over time using an exponential function to model time preference, thereby bounding the expected long-term reward. In contrast, in economics and psychology, it has been shown that humans often adopt a hyperbolic discounting scheme, which is optimal when a specific task termination time distribution is assumed.

title: Efficient On-Device Session-Based Recommendation Journal: TOIS Volume: 1 1 1 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Thanks: This work was supported by the Australian Research Council Future Fellowship (Grant No. FT210100624), the Discovery Project (Grant No. DP190101985), and the Discovery Early Career
creator: Xin Xia, Junliang Yu, Qinyong Wang, Chaoqun Yang, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xin Xia, Junliang Yu, Qinyong Wang, Chaoqun Yang, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin. On-device session-based recommendation systems have been achieving increasing attention on account of the low energy/resource consumption and privacy protection while providing promising recommendation performance. To fit the powerful neural session-based recommendation models in resource-constrained mobile devices, tensor-train decomposition and its variants have been widely applied to reduce memory footprint by decomposing the embedding table into smaller tensors, showing great potential in compressing recommendation models.

title: Isometric, symmetric and isosymmetric commuting d d -tuples of Banach space operators
creator: B.P. Duggal, I.H. Kim
description: Abstract Generalising the definition to commuting d d -tuples of operators, a number of authors have considered structural properties of m m -isometric, n n -symmetric and ( m , n ) (m,n) -isosymmetric commuting d d -tuples in the recent past.

title: Clubs and their applications
creator: Vito Napolitano, Olga Polverino, Paolo Santonastaso, Ferdinando Zullo
description: Abstract . Clubs of rank k k are well-celebrated objects in finite geometries introduced by Fancsali and Sziklai in 2006. After the connection with a special type of arcs known as KM-arcs, they renewed their interest. This paper aims to study clubs of rank n n in PG ⁡ ( 1 , q n ) \mathrm{PG}(1,q^{n}) .

title: PCA-based Channel Estimation for MIMO Communications
creator: Jonathan Aguiar Soares, Kayol Soares Mayer, Pedro Benevenuto Valadares, and Dalton Soares Arantes
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Aguiar Soares, Kayol Soares Mayer, Pedro Benevenuto Valadares, and Dalton Soares Arantes. In multiple-input multiple-output communications, channel estimation is paramount to keep base stations and users on track. This paper proposes a novel PCA-based – principal component analysis – channel estimation approach for MIMO orthogonal frequency division multiplexing systems.

title: The volume conjecture for polyhedra implies the Stoker conjecture
creator: Giulio Belletti
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Giulio Belletti. We show that the Volume Conjecture for polyhedra implies a weak version of the Stoker Conjecture; in turn we prove that this weak version of the Stoker conjecture implies the Stoker conjecture. The main tool used is an extension of a result of Montcouquiol and Weiss, saying that dihedral angles are local coordinates for compact polyhedra with angles ≤ π \leq\pi .

title: Extremal ternary self-dual codes of length 36 and symmetric 2- ( 36 , 15 , 6 ) (36,15,6) designs with an automorphism of order 2
creator: Sanja Rukavina, Vladimir D. Tonchev
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sanja Rukavina, Vladimir D. Tonchev. In this note we report the classification of all symmetric 2- ( 36 , 15 , 6 ) (36,15,6) designs that admit an automorphism of order 2 and their incidence matrices generate an extremal ternary self-dual code. It is shown that up to isomorphism, there exists only one such design, having a full automorphism group of order 24, and the ternary code spanned by its incidence matrix is equivalent to the Pless symmetry code. * Corresponding author.

title: Star-forming early- and quiescent late-type galaxies in the local Universe
creator: E.-D. Paspaliaris, E. M. Xilouris, A. Nersesian, S. Bianchi, I. Georgantopoulos, V. A. Masoura, G. E. Magdis, M. Plionis
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by E.-D. Paspaliaris, E. M. Xilouris, A. Nersesian, S. Bianchi, I. Georgantopoulos, V. A. Masoura, G. E. Magdis, M. Plionis. The general consensus is that late-type galaxies undergo intense star-formation activity while early-type galaxies are mostly inactive. We question this general rule and investigate the existence of star-forming early-type and quenched late-type galaxies in the local universe.

title: Accelerating hypersonic reentry simulations using deep learning-based hybridization (with guarantees) Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
creator: Paul Novello, Gaël Poëtte, David Lugato, Simon Peluchon, Pietro Marco Congedo
description: Abstract In this paper, we are interested in the acceleration of numerical simulations. We focus on a hypersonic planetary reentry problem whose simulation involves coupling fluid dynamics and chemical reactions. Simulating chemical reactions takes most of the computational time but, on the other hand, cannot be avoided to obtain accurate predictions.

title: Polynomial time computable functions over the reals characterized using discrete ordinary differential equations
creator: Manon Blanc, Olivier Bournez
description: Abstract The class of functions from the integers to the integers computable in polynomial time has been characterized recently using discrete ordinary differential equations (ODE), also known as finite differences. In the framework of ordinary differential equations, it is very natural to try to extend the approach to classes of functions over the reals, and not only over the integers.

title: Forecasting the success of the WEAVE Wide-Field Cluster Survey on the extraction of the cosmic web filaments around galaxy clusters 2022 Forecasting the success of the WEAVE Wide-Field Cluster Survey on the extraction of the cosmic web filaments around galaxy clusters – C
creator: Daniel J. Cornwell, Ulrike Kuchner, Alfonso Aragón-Salamanca, Meghan E. Gray, Frazer R. Pearce, J. Alfonso L. Aguerri, Weiguang Cui, J. Méndez-Abreu, Luis Peralta de Arriba, Scott C. Trager, School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Nottingham, Nottingham NG7 2RD, UK Instituto de Astrofísica de
description: Abstract Next-generation wide-field spectroscopic surveys will observe the infall regions around large numbers of galaxy clusters with high sampling rates for the first time. Here we assess the feasibility of extracting the large-scale cosmic web around clusters using forthcoming observations, given realistic observational constraints.

title: Feature-based Learning for Diverse and Privacy-Preserving Counterfactual Explanations Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 6–10, 2023; Long Beach, CA, USA Proceedings of the 29th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data
creator: Vy Vo, Trung Le, Van Nguyen, He Zhao, Edwin V. Bonilla, Gholamreza Haffari, Dinh Phung
description: Abstract . Interpretable machine learning seeks to understand the reasoning process of complex black-box systems that are long notorious for lack of explainability. One flourishing approach is through counterfactual explanations, which provide suggestions on what a user can do to alter an outcome.

title: WeightedSHAP: analyzing and improving Shapley based feature attributions
creator: Yongchan Kwon, James Zou
description: Abstract Shapley value is a popular approach for measuring the influence of individual features. While Shapley feature attribution is built upon desiderata from game theory, some of its constraints may be less natural in certain machine learning settings, leading to unintuitive model interpretation. In particular, the Shapley value uses the same weight for all marginal contributions—i.e.

title: Signatures of excited monopolium
creator: Huner Fanchiotti, Carlos A. García Canal, Marco Traini, Vicente Vento
description: Abstract We study electromagnetic properties of particles with magnetic moment and no charge using their behavior when traversing coils and solenoids. These particles via the Faraday-Lenz law create a current whose energy we calculate. We analyze both the case of very long lived, almost stable, particles and those with a finite lifetime.

title: Sentiment is all you need to win US Presidential elections
creator: Sovesh MohapatraUniversity of Massachusetts Amherst soveshmohapa@umass.edu, Somesh MohapatraMassachusetts Institute of Technology someshm@mit.edu
description: Abstract Election speeches play an integral role in communicating the vision and mission of the candidates. From lofty promises to mud-slinging, the electoral candidate accounts for all. However, there remains an open question about what exactly wins over the voters.

title: B c B_{c} enhancement with non-thermalized bottom quarks in nuclear collisions at Large Hadron Collider
creator: Jiaxing Zhao, Pengfei Zhuang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jiaxing Zhao, Pengfei Zhuang. We study B c B_{c} production in high-energy nuclear collisions in a transport approach with dissociation and regeneration at finite temperatures. Due to the rare production in p+p collisions and the strong combination of uncorrelated c c and b ¯ \bar{b} quarks in the quark-gluon plasma, the B c B_{c} yield is significantly enhanced in the nuclear collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

title: Autonomous and non-autonomous unbounded attractors in evolutionary problems
creator: Jakub Banaśkiewicz 1, Alexandre N. Carvalho 2, Juan Garcia-Fuentes 3, Piotr Kalita 1,3
description: Abstract . If the semigroup is slowly non-dissipative, i.e., its solutions can diverge to infinity as time tends to infinity, one still can study its dynamics via the approach by the unbounded attractors - the counterpart of the classical notion of global attractors. We continue the development of this theory started by Chepyzhov and Goritskii [ CG92 ] .

title: Improved Mixed Dark Matter Halo Model for Ultralight Axions
creator: Sophie M. L. Vogt 1,2, David J. E. Marsh 3, Alex Laguë 4,5,6,7
description: Abstract We present a complete halo model for mixed dark matter composed of cold dark matter (CDM) and ultralight axion-like particles (ULAs). Our model treats ULAs as a biased tracer of CDM, in analogy to treatments of massive neutrinos and neutral hydrogen.

title: Deterministic non-adaptive contention resolution on a shared channel Thanks: A preliminary version of this paper appeared in the proceedings of the 39th IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems (ICDCS 2019).
creator: Gianluca De Marco, Dariusz R. Kowalski, Grzegorz Stachowiak
description: Abstract In a multiple access channel, autonomous stations are able to transmit and listen to a shared device. A fundamental problem, called contention resolution , is to allow any station to successfully deliver its message by resolving the conflicts that arise when several stations transmit simultaneously.

title: Lotka-Volterra Competition Models on Finite Graphs Thanks: 1 School of Mathematics and Statistics, Henan University, Kaifeng, Henan 475004, P. R. China. Thanks: 2 School of Mathematics and Statistics, Jiangsu Normal University, Xuzhou, 221116, Jiangsu Province, China. Thanks: Emails: yuanyhu@mail.us
creator: Yuanyang Hu 1, Chengxia Lei 2
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuanyang Hu 1, Chengxia Lei 2. In this paper, we study three two competing species Lotka-Volterra competition models on finite connected graphs, with Dirichlet, Neumann or no boundary conditions. We get that when time goes to infinity, either one specie extincts while the other becomes surviving or both competing species coexist, which depend crucially on the strengh of species’ competitiveness and the size of the initial population under the Neumann boundary condition and the condition that there is no boundary condition.

title: A constrained mean curvature flow and Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities
creator: Xinqun Mei, Guofang Wang, Liangjun Weng
description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xinqun Mei, Guofang Wang, Liangjun Weng. In this article, we study a locally constrained mean curvature flow for star-shaped hypersurfaces with capillary boundary in the half-space. We prove its long-time existence and the global convergence to a spherical cap. Furthermore, the capillary quermassintegrals defined in [ 29 ] evolve monotonically along the flow, and hence we establish a class of new Alexandrov-Fenchel inequalities for convex hypersurfaces with capillary boundary in the half-space. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 53C21, Secondary 35K55, 35K93.

title: Characterizing Uncertainty in the Visual Text Analysis Pipeline
creator: Pantea Haghighatkhah ♢, Mennatallah El-Assady ♣, Jean-Daniel Fekete ♠, Narges Mahyar ‡, Carita Paradis §, Vasiliki Simaki §, Bettina Speckmann ♢
description: Abstract Current visual text analysis approaches rely on sophisticated processing pipelines. Each step of such a pipeline potentially amplifies any uncertainties from the previous step. To ensure the comprehensibility and interoperability of the results, it is of paramount importance to clearly communicate the uncertainty not only of the output but also within the pipeline.

title: Measurement of the Neutron Cross Section on Argon Between 95 and 720 MeV
creator: S. Martynenko, B. Bhandari, J. Bian, K. Bilton, C. Callahan, J. Chaves, H. Chen, D. Cline, R. L. Cooper, D. L. Danielson, J. Danielson, N. Dokania, S. Elliott, S. Fernandes, S. Gardiner, G. Garvey, V. Gehman, F. Giuliani, S. Glavin, M. Gold, C. Grant, E. Guardincerri, T. Haines, A. Higuera, J. Y. Ji
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by S. Martynenko, B. Bhandari, J. Bian, K. Bilton, C. Callahan, J. Chaves, H. Chen, D. Cline, R. L. Cooper, D. L. Danielson, J. Danielson, N. Dokania, S. Elliott, S. Fernandes, S. Gardiner, G. Garvey, V. Gehman, F. Giuliani, S. Glavin, M. Gold, C. Grant, E. Guardincerri, T. Haines, A. Higuera, J. Y. Ji. We report an extended measurement of the neutron cross section on argon in the energy range of 95-720 MeV.

title: Joint Stochastic Model for Electric Load, Solar and Wind Power at Asset Level and Monte Carlo Scenario Generation
creator: René Carmona & Xinshuo Yang
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by René Carmona & Xinshuo Yang. For the purpose of Monte Carlo scenario generation, we propose a graphical model for the joint distribution of wind power and electricity demand in a given region. To conform with the practice in the electric power industry, we assume that point forecasts are provided exogenously, and concentrate on the modeling of the deviations from these forecasts instead of modeling the actual quantities of interest.

title: Jubileo: An Open-Source Robot and Framework for Research in Human-Robot Social Interaction
creator: Jair A. Bottega, Victor A. Kich, Alisson H. Kolling, Jardel D. S. Dyonisio, Pedro L. Corçaque, Rodrigo da S. Guerra, Daniel F. T. Gamarra
description: Abstract Human-robot interaction (HRI) is essential to the widespread use of robots in daily life. Robots will eventually be able to carry out a variety of duties in human civilization through effective social interaction. Creating straightforward and understandable interfaces to engage with robots as they start to proliferate in the personal workspace is essential.

title: Personalized Game Difficulty Prediction Using Factorization Machines Conference: The 35th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology; October 29-November 2, 2022; Bend, OR, USA CCS: Human-centered computing User models CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer interaction (HCI
creator: Jeppe Theiss Kristensen, Christian Guckelsberger, Paolo Burelli, Perttu Hämäläinen
description: Abstract . The accurate and personalized estimation of task difficulty provides many opportunities for optimizing user experience. However, user diversity makes such difficulty estimation hard, in that empirical measurements from some user sample do not necessarily generalize to others. In this paper, we contribute a new approach for personalized difficulty estimation of game levels, borrowing methods from content recommendation.

title: Mine yOur owN Anatomy: Revisiting Medical Image Segmentation with Extremely Limited Labels
creator: Chenyu You ∗, Weicheng Dai ∗, Fenglin Liu, Yifei Min, Nicha C. Dvornek, Xiaoxiao Li, David A. Clifton, Lawrence Staib, and James S. Duncan
description: Abstract Recent studies on contrastive learning have achieved remarkable performance solely by leveraging few labels in the context of medical image segmentation. Existing methods mainly focus on instance discrimination and invariant mapping ( i.e. , pulling positive samples closer and negative samples apart in the feature space).

title: Open quantum dynamics for plant motions
creator: Dorje C. Brody 1,2
description: Abstract Stochastic Schrödinger equations that govern the dynamics of open quantum systems are given by the equations for signal processing. In particular, the Brownian motion that drives the wave function of the system does not represent noise, but provides purely the arrival of new information.

title: Norms of embeddings between quadratically weighted spaces of holomorphic functions
creator: Joe Viola
description: Abstract . We consider spaces of holomorphic functions which are square-integrable against a Gaussian weight, which appear in the theory of metaplectic FBI–Bargmann transforms. We identify the operator norm of embeddings between two such spaces, by relating these embeddings to Fourier integral operators with complex phase. 1.

title: CrossDTR: Cross-view and Depth-guided Transformers for 3D Object Detection
creator: Ching-Yu Tseng, Yi-Rong Chen, Hsin-Ying Lee, Tsung-Han Wu, Wen-Chin Chen, Winston H. Hsu
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ching-Yu Tseng, Yi-Rong Chen, Hsin-Ying Lee, Tsung-Han Wu, Wen-Chin Chen, Winston H. Hsu. To achieve accurate 3D object detection at a low cost for autonomous driving, many multi-camera methods have been proposed and solved the occlusion problem of monocular approaches. However, due to the lack of accurate estimated depth, existing multi-camera methods often generate multiple bounding boxes along a ray of depth direction for difficult small objects such as pedestrians, resulting in an extremely low recall.

title: Rotating Solar Models in Agreement with Helioseismic Results and Updated Neutrino Fluxes
creator: Wuming Yang
description: Abstract Standard solar models (SSMs) constructed in accordance with old solar abundances are in reasonable agreement with seismically inferred results, but SSMs with new low-metal abundances disagree with the seismically inferred results. The constraints of neutrino fluxes on solar models exist in parallel with those of helioseismic results. The solar neutrino fluxes were updated by Borexino Collaboration.

title: More infinite classes of APN-like Power Functions
creator: Longjiang Qu, Kangquan Li
description: Abstract In the literature, there are many APN-like functions that generalize the APN properties or are similar to APN functions, e.g. locally-APN functions, 0-APN functions or those with boomerang uniformity 2. In this paper, we study the problem of constructing infinite classes of APN-like but not APN power functions.

title: A pathwise Regularization by noise phenomenon for the evolutionary p p -Laplace equation
creator: Florian Bechtold, Jörn Wichmann
description:
A 2022 arXiv research paper by Florian Bechtold, Jörn Wichmann. We study an evolutionary p p -Laplace problem whose potential is subject to a translation in time. Provided the trajectory along which the potential is translated admits a sufficiently regular local time, we establish existence of solutions to the problem for singular potentials for which a priori bounds in classical approaches break down, thereby establishing a pathwise regularization by noise phenomena for this non-linear problem.
